extracted.intended_audience: users who write answers on Mathematics Stack Exchange (answerers/contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing helpful, well-formed answers to questions on Mathematics Stack Exchange, including what to include, what to avoid, and community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the question carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: "What is the question asking for? Make sure your answer provides that – or at least a viable alternative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your answer can say “don’t do that,” but it should also say “try this instead.” Any answer that fully addresses at least part of the question is helpful and can get the asker going in the right direction. State any limitations, assumptions or simplifications in your answer. Brevity is acceptable, but fuller explanations are better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context for links
rubrics_metrics.description: "Links to external resources are encouraged, but please add context around the link so your fellow users will have some idea what it is and why it’s there."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always quote the most relevant part of an important link, in case the external resource is unreachable or goes permanently offline. Links to other websites should always be helpful, but avoid making it necessary to click on them as much as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share research and troubleshooting (Have the same problem?)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Help us find a solution by researching the problem. So long as you fully answer at least a part of the original question, then you can contribute the results of your research and anything additional you’ve tried."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you couldn't fully solve it, report what you've tried so the next person has more to go on. You can also support the question by voting it up or setting a bounty so it gets more attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to the best of your ability (clear writing and editability)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Answers with correct spelling, punctuation, and grammar are easier to read. They also tend to get upvoted more frequently."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We don't expect every answer to be perfect, but strive for clear writing; you can always go back and edit your answer to improve it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay it forward (constructive gratitude and participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Saying 'thanks' is appreciated, but it doesn’t answer the question."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of leaving a thank-you comment, vote up the answers that helped you most and consider contributing your own answers to help others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer well-asked questions (avoid answering unsuitable questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Not all questions can or should be answered here. Save yourself some frustration and avoid trying to answer questions which..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not answer questions that are: unclear or lacking specific details; solicit opinions rather than facts; have already been asked and answered many times (duplicates); require too much guidance for you to answer in full or request multiple questions; or are not about math as defined in the help center. Instead, consider editing the question to improve clarity or refrain from answering until it's suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit the question you're answering to improve clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Don't forget that you can edit the question you're answering to improve the clarity and focus – this can reduce the chances of the question being closed or deleted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question is unclear but salvageable, make focused edits (or suggest them) so answers will be on-target and the post will remain visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be civil and maintain a friendly tone
rubrics_metrics.description: "Always be polite and have fun. It’s fine to disagree and express concern, but please be civil."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember there is a real human on the other end; criticize ideas, not people, and keep interactions respectful.
